Country-specific data patches

Source: R/country-patches.R
country_patches.Rd

Three country-list rules of the build work around idiosyncrasies of specific national data sources — these are data-source patches, not general econometric rules (steps 6, 8 and 17 of build_accounts_indicators()). They are kept here as one explicit, documented table instead of scattered if (country %in% c(...)) chains, so extending them as more countries join the project only requires editing this table.

Usage

country_patches

Format

A named list with three character vectors:

rescale_to_thousands

Countries whose raw financial variables are supplied in EUR and divided by 1000, unless the configuration says otherwise (config_scaleup()'s financials_unit): PT, ES, RO, SI, HU.

non_euro

Countries whose turnover needs converting to national currency via exchange_rates.dta (used to detect the "20-200-20" employment/turnover jump pattern in national-currency terms): DK, HU, RO, CA, HR.

aggregate_small_regions

Countries where TL2 regions with a thin count of HGET10 scalers get coarsened up to the TL1 level: AT, CA, HU, IT, NL, ES, RO.

trade_values_in_eur

Trade package: countries whose trade_value is supplied in EUR and divided by 1000, unless the configuration says otherwise (config_scaleup()'s trade_value_unit): PT, HU.
